card: Adds Cap'n Proto definitions and proxy wrappers to expose the `interfaces::Chain` and `interfaces::Handler` interfaces over IPC on `bitcoin-node`. Currently, the `Chain` interface can only be invoked within the same process, blocking multi-process wallet separation. This is an explicit prerequisite for #10102 and #19460 to run wallet logic in a separate executable.
evidence: PR description: "The changes in this PR allow a `bitcoin-node` process to be controlled over a socket... This PR is a dependency of #10102 which allows the wallet code to run in a separate process and use the `Chain` interface."
problem: Bitcoin Core's `interfaces::Chain` interface can only be called in-process. Out-of-process components, such as a separated `bitcoin-wallet` process, cannot access node chain services or listen to block and transaction notifications over IPC.
scope_notes: Includes a significant subtree update to `src/ipc/libmultiprocess` (bumping to v14) alongside new Cap'n Proto schemas and proxy glue code in `src/ipc/capnp/`. Also makes minor signature adjustments to `interfaces::Chain` in `src/interfaces/chain.h`.
summary: Adds Cap'n Proto serialization and proxy wrappers for Bitcoin Core's `interfaces::Chain` and `interfaces::Handler` interfaces, and exposes the `Chain` interface via IPC on `bitcoin-node`. This allows out-of-process clients connecting via UNIX sockets (`-ipcbind`) or socket pairs (`-ipcfd`) to query chain state, register notifications, and execute chain methods. It also updates the `src/ipc/libmultiprocess` subtree to version 14.
